answer:
**Jensen's inequality explains why moving a nonlinear function outside an expectation changes the result.** For a convex function, the function lies above a supporting line at the mean. Taking expectations of that line cancels its linear displacement term, giving $g(E[X])\leq E[g(X)]$. Log is concave, so its inequality points the other way. [2](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html)

A latent-variable model's evidence integrates over z, which can be hard to evaluate. Introduce a tractable q(z|x), write the evidence as an expectation of p(x,z)/q(z|x), then apply concavity of log. This produces a computable lower bound: expected reconstruction log likelihood minus KL from q to the prior. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.6114)

**The bound has an exact gap.** Log evidence minus ELBO equals KL from the approximate posterior q to the true posterior. If they match, the gap is zero; if q cannot represent the posterior, the gap can remain positive.

Support and integrability assumptions are necessary for the rearrangement. Optimizing the ELBO improves a lower bound, not directly a guarantee of sharp samples or exact inference. The variational family and decoder determine what compromises the model can make.

**Technical details and references.**

For differentiable convex $g$, the supporting-line inequality is $g(x)\ge g(m)+g'(m)(x-m)$ at $m=\mathbb E[X]$. Taking expectations cancels the linear term, giving Jensen's inequality. Subgradients extend the argument to suitable nondifferentiable convex functions. Concave $\log$ reverses the inequality. [2](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html)

Write $\log p_\theta(x)=\log\mathbb E_{q_\phi(z|x)}[p_\theta(x,z)/q_\phi(z|x)]$. Applying concavity yields $\mathbb E_q[\log p_\theta(x,z)-\log q_\phi(z|x)]$, which expands into the expected reconstruction log likelihood minus $D_{KL}(q_\phi(z|x)\|p(z))$. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.6114)

The gap is $D_{KL}(q_\phi(z|x)\|p_\theta(z|x))\ge0$. Equality holds when the variational posterior equals the true posterior, subject to support and integrability requirements. Optimizing the bound jointly improves the generative model and its approximate posterior; a restricted variational family can leave a nonzero inference gap.
